title: Windows and PowerShell
summary: New-SelfSignedCertificate, the Cert: drive, PFX export and import, certutil, certreq and dotnet dev-certs.

steps.title: New-SelfSignedCertificate, including a chain
body: On Windows you rarely need openssl. PowerShell makes certificates straight into the certificate store:
# a dev root that may sign one level of certificates
# a TLS leaf signed by that root
- `-DnsName`: every name goes in the SAN; the first also becomes the subject CN
- `-Signer`: sign with another certificate (which must have its private key) instead of self-signing
- `-TextExtension`: raw extensions by OID: `2.5.29.19` Basic Constraints, `2.5.29.37` EKU, `2.5.29.17` SAN
- It always writes to a store (`My` = Personal). `-NotAfter` defaults to one year.

steps.prompt: Complete the command for a one-year `shop.example` certificate in your Personal store.
steps.explain: `-DnsName` (not `-Subject`) is what gives you a SAN. `-CertStoreLocation` is a `Cert:` drive path.

steps.title: The Cert: drive, PFX and CER files
body: # browse and filter (Cert:\CurrentUser\Root = trusted roots, \CA = intermediates)
Format-List Subject, Issuer, NotAfter, Thumbprint, HasPrivateKey
# export: PFX = certificate + private key (password protected), CER = certificate only (DER)

steps.prompt: Match each cmdlet to what it does.
pairs: writes certificate **and private key** to a password-protected file
puts a PFX's certificate and key into a store
makes the current user trust a root

steps.prompt: Your Personal store holds these three certificates. What does the command print? (One subject per line, in store order.)
steps.explain: The cutoff is 2030-07-01. Both leaves expire before it (one has, in fact, already expired: the filter catches those too); the root does not.

steps.title: certutil, certreq and dotnet dev-certs
body: `certutil` ships with every Windows and reads files without touching the store:
certutil -dump shop.cer                    # decode a certificate (like openssl x509 -text)
certutil -dump shop.pfx                    # inspect a PFX (asks for the password)
certutil -verify -urlfetch shop.cer        # build the chain, fetch AIA/CRL/OCSP, report errors
certutil -hashfile shop.cer SHA256         # SHA-256 of the file (= fingerprint for a DER file)
certutil -addstore -f Root dojo-root.cer   # trust a root machine-wide (admin)
`certreq` makes a CSR from an `.inf` file (`certreq -new request.inf shop.csr`) and submits it to an Active Directory CA (`certreq -submit`).
dotnet dev-certs https --check --trust     # is there one, and is it trusted?
dotnet dev-certs https --trust             # create it and trust it (CurrentUser\Root)

steps.prompt: Built into Windows, or an openssl/Linux command?
`dotnet dev-certs https --trust` on Windows. What does it do?
options: Creates the localhost development certificate if needed and adds it to the current user's Trusted Root store (after a confirmation prompt)
Downloads a certificate from Let's Encrypt
Installs a machine-wide root for every user
steps.explain: The dev cert is self-signed for `localhost`; trusting it means putting it in `Cert:\CurrentUser\Root`. Use `--export-path` to hand it to Docker or a Linux box.

steps.title: Find certificates that expire soon
prompt: Write `List<string> ExpiringWithin(X509Certificate2Collection certs, DateTime nowUtc, int days)` returning the subjects of certificates whose `NotAfter` is before `nowUtc + days`, sorted by `NotAfter` (earliest first). Already-expired certificates count too.
`NotAfter` is **local** time; `nowUtc` is UTC. Convert before comparing. (No store: you get a collection, so this runs anywhere.)
starter: List<string> ExpiringWithin(X509Certificate2Collection certs, DateTime nowUtc, int days)
solution: List<string> ExpiringWithin(X509Certificate2Collection certs, DateTime nowUtc, int days)
template: dojoCerts.Add(DojoCert("CN=Dojo Root", null, true, nbYear: 2030, naYear: 2045));
Dojo.Eq("within 365 days of 2034-06-01", new List<string> { "CN=gone.example", "CN=soon.example" }, ExpiringWithin(dojoCerts, dojoNow, 365));
Dojo.Eq("within 800 days", new List<string> { "CN=gone.example", "CN=soon.example", "CN=later.example" }, ExpiringWithin(dojoCerts, dojoNow, 800));
Dojo.Eq("nothing within 0 days of 2030-06-01", new List<string>(), ExpiringWithin(dojoCerts, new DateTime(2030, 6, 1, 0, 0, 0, DateTimeKind.Utc), 0));
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);

steps.title: Export-PfxCertificate and Import-PfxCertificate
prompt: Write the two halves of a PFX round trip, without any certificate store:
- `byte[] ExportPfx(X509Certificate2 cert, string password)`, like `Export-PfxCertificate`: the certificate **with its private key**, password protected
- `X509Certificate2 ImportPfx(byte[] pfx, string password)`, like `Import-PfxCertificate` but into memory: use `X509CertificateLoader.LoadPkcs12`

A wrong password must throw (`LoadPkcs12` does that for you: let the `CryptographicException` escape). `ExportPfx` must refuse a certificate without a private key: throw `InvalidOperationException`, the error you would get from `Export-PfxCertificate` on a public-only certificate.
solution: if (!cert.HasPrivateKey) throw new InvalidOperationException("the certificate has no private key");
template: var dojoCert = DojoCert("CN=shop.example", DojoCert("CN=Dojo Root", null, true), false, "shop.example");
Dojo.Eq("round trip keeps the subject", "CN=shop.example", dojoBack.Subject);
Dojo.Eq("round trip keeps the private key", true, dojoBack.HasPrivateKey);
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("a public-only certificate cannot become a PFX", () => ExportPfx(dojoPublic, "pw"));
static X509Certificate2 DojoCert(string subject, X509Certificate2? issuer, bool isCa, string? dns = null, string? eku = null, int nbYear = 2030, int naYear = 2035)
var req = new CertificateRequest(subject, key, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256);
req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509KeyUsageExtension(isCa ? X509KeyUsageFlags.KeyCertSign | X509KeyUsageFlags.CrlSign : X509KeyUsageFlags.DigitalSignature, true));
if (dns != null) { var b = new SubjectAlternativeNameBuilder(); foreach (var d in dns.Split(',')) b.AddDnsName(d); req.CertificateExtensions.Add(b.Build()); }
if (eku != null) req.CertificateExtensions.Add(new X509EnhancedKeyUsageExtension(new OidCollection { new Oid(eku) }, false));
using var pub = req.Create(issuer, nb, na, serial);
